page.layout: One printed page, numbered 64 at the head. A woodcut ornamental strip at the top. Below it a full-width heading (AD HENRICVM III. / Nauarrae Regem.), then one text block of verse with a historiated initial A at the left, the lines set in stanza-like groups. A short signature word at the lower right ("Milesve") under the last line.

l.i: Quo te celebrem carmine? qua Lyra
Quem non profanis, quæ rotat arcibus

page.notes: The initial A is a large decorated woodcut letter; read as "A", joined to "NTIQVA" as "ANTIQVA". The line "Itaque Magnatum, nec arma" is printed as "{f}raque" with a long-f-like initial in the scan; it is read here as "sraque" in the original and transcribed as "Itaque" with [?]. Line reading "Itaque Magnatum" should be checked: "{s}raque Magnatum" is likely "fraque Magnatum" (fraque = and also). The letter in "Quem" is clear. The ornamental strip and the signature word "Milesve" (printed at lower right, set apart from the verse) are the only other printed elements. The printed word "Milesve" is in italic and is a catchword-like line; it is recorded in main_text as the final italic line.
